results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons, parts, subclasses, tracts, lineage clones, images, and expression patterns, with over 60,000 records available.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including gamma Kenyon cells. According to the VFB database, there are three main subtypes that project their axons to different lobes, specifically the alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, as referenced in Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. The VFB database also provides additional information on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. According to the VFB database, its cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind (as noted in VFB and VFB, which cite Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017). LPLC2 has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli. The activity of LPLC2 elicits a jump escape response. VFB holds information on 163 neuron types, including LPLC2, which is identified by the ID VFB_jrch0fva.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). According to VFB, it has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. The giant fiber neuron has a large descending axon and arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. There is one of these cells per hemisphere, and its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, as identified by Koto et al. (1981) and Namiki et al. (2018). The large descending axon is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective, as noted by Power (1948) and Koto et al. (1981). 

VFB holds extensive data on the giant fiber neuron, including [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. Available driver lines include P{VT046265-GAL4}, which has a characterized expression pattern. Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Sturner et al. (2025).
